title: Toccata and Fugue in D minor: Stokowski and Schenk
work: Toccata and Fugue in D minor, BWV 565 — opening
question: Stokowski’s orchestra and Schenk’s organ play Bach’s opening flourish and the toccata passages that follow.
intro: At Philadelphia’s Academy of Music on 6 April 1927, Stokowski recorded his orchestral version of Bach’s D minor Toccata and Fugue. He gave the organist’s flourishes to a large orchestra that included six horns, four trumpets and four trombones. Ninety years later, Norbert Schenk recorded the work on the church organ in Solms-Albshausen, with one player at the instrument.

recordings.label: Leopold Stokowski, 1927
recordings.note: Stokowski conducts the Philadelphia Orchestra in his own transcription, which enlarges the organ’s flourishes with a large brass section.

recordings.label: Norbert Schenk, 2017
recordings.note: Schenk plays the Protestant church organ in Solms-Albshausen; hands and feet supply the running notes and the bass beneath them.

passages.label: Opening flourish in octaves
passages.note: The opening flourish descends in octaves, then stops, and a rest follows.

passages.label: Held chord under fast line
passages.note: Notes accumulate into a held chord, and the fast line now runs over it.

passages.label: Runs alternating with held chords
passages.note: The toccata alternates rapid runs with passages that stop on sustained chords.
